text.p: Cyprus's finance minister on Thursday announced tax breaks for investors and companies to revive interest in the 10-month old bourse.

"I briefed the board of the Cyprus Stock Exchange of our decision that for reasons of taxation, companies on the bourse will get the same treatment public companies get," Finance Minister Christodoulos Christodoulou told reporters.

Under the new regulations, 30 percent of investments in new companies listing on the exchange will be tax deductible and tax exemptions will be allowed on the first 1200 pounds ($2,400) paid in dividends.
"This move affects investors in a new company floating on the stock exchange," bourse director Nondas Metaxas told Reuters.

The general index of the bourse, which started operating last March after years of unofficial over-the-counter transactions, recently fell to a low of 75.33 points. Shares of 41 registered companies are traded.
Christodoulou said the price decline after the opening of the bourse was primarily a correction of high levels the bourse soared to in the months preceding the official opening of the exchange.
"The CSE is working very satisfactorily," he said after meeting bourse officials.
Bourse chairman Dinos Papadopoulos said the CSE and the government were in the process of looking at new ways to encourage companies to float on the exchange.
Christodoulou, who met for an hour with the CSE board, said that other suggestions made by the bourse which also covered taxation issues were being studied.
He said the government stuck by its intention to float five-year development bonds on the CSE, a move which many analysts think will be the driving force behind the bourse in months to come.
Flotation of the bonds is due this year, though no dates have been given yet.
